Documented shortcuts (docs/SEARCH_LIMITATIONS.md)

Cube lands (line-composed land grammar): automatic mana payment, hand abilities, life-costed taps — 2026-09-27, `feature/cube-lands`1. **Automatic payment only uses a land's `produces` set.** Lands built by the line-composed grammar set `mana_only_from_produces=True`: a land contributes to `can_pay_cost` / `auto_tap_for_cost` only through its free (or life-costed) `{T}: Add` production. Mana abilities with any other cost or shape — Gaea's Cradle / Tolarian Academy (scaling), Mishra's Workshop (spend restriction), Sunken Ruins (filter, `{U/B}` input), Gemstone Mine (counter cost), Starting Town's `{T}, Pay 1 life: Add one mana of any color`, Arena of Glory's exert ability — are explicit mana abilities, usable only by activating them (which `legal_actions` offers only in a sorcery window, like every activated ability) and floating the mana. So none of them can pay for an instant-speed cast.

Documented shortcuts (docs/SEARCH_LIMITATIONS.md)

Rust-parity-pinned lossy legacy spells**What the shortcut is.** The compositional phrase grammar models "target creature or planeswalker", "counter target spell unless its controller pays {N}", and other surfaces faithfully, but five Edge-of-Eternities-era spells were claimed earlier through lossy legacy recognizers (planeswalker target arm dropped, pay-or-counter tax dropped, riders dropped, or only one of several modes kept) and their simplified models are pinned by cross-engine parity tests against the Rust engine: Divert Disaster, Don't Make a Sound, Archenemy's Charm, Scorching Dragonfire, Break Down the Door (plus Get Out / Untimely Malfunction for the single-parseable-mode modal fallback). While one of those names is being parsed the compositional grammar is switched off, so they keep the legacy models. Every other card with the same printed surfaces (including the cube's Mana Leak, Sear, Baleful Mastery, Unholy Heat, Mine Collapse, …) now parses faithfully, and the single-parseable-mode fallback no longer claims non-legacy modal spells (Suplex, Sheoldred's Edict must parse every mode).
Printed alternative costs share the `cast_for_free` action variant**What the shortcut is.** CR 118.9 alternative costs (Force of Will, Daze, Force of Negation / Vigor, Snuff Out, Mine Collapse, Baleful Mastery, Overload on Damn / Winds of Abandon) ride the casting substrate's existing `CastSpell(cast_for_free=True)` variant — the same one `alt_casting`'s pitch costs and conditional free casts use — so there is ONE cast-time alternative-cost path and the action encoding is unchanged (the codec already has a `cast_for_free` slot). The variant means "cast for an alternative cost" rather than naming WHICH one: a free-cast permission wins, and when a card prints several payable alternatives the caster's agent picks among them with `choose_mode` inside the cast. No printed card in either pool has two payable alternatives at once, so today the variant is unambiguous. Two further approximations: (1) `search/_player_capabilities.py`'s priority short-circuit only checks mana costs, so with that heuristic enabled a player whose only castable card is a free-cast (e.g. Force of Will with no untapped lands) can be skipped; (2) when several candidates can pay an alternative cost the pick reuses existing hooks: `choose_discard` for the exiled hand card (as `alt_casting.pay_pitch_cost` does), `choose_sacrifice` for the returned / sacrificed permanent.

Documented shortcuts (docs/SEARCH_LIMITATIONS.md)

PowerLSV cube creatures bucket (red / multicolor / colorless) — engine shortcuts (2026-09-27, `feature/cube-creatures-rmc`)7. **Graveyard watch sweeps.** Blightsteel Colossus's "would be put into a graveyard from anywhere → shuffle into library" is applied directly when it leaves the battlefield (`turn.move_off_battlefield`). From other zones (discard, mill) it is applied by `rmc.sweep_graveyard_watch` at the next state-based-action pass, so the card sits in the graveyard briefly (a graveyard count read in between sees it). Emrakul's "is put into a graveyard from anywhere" trigger is detected by the same sweep (`Player.graveyard_arrival_watch`).

Documented shortcuts (docs/SEARCH_LIMITATIONS.md)

Cube spells-B: card-flow / casting-substrate shortcuts — 2026-09-27, `feature/cube-spells-b`1. **"In any order" orderings are not offered.** Scry (`bottom_choice=True`) keeps the kept cards on top and the bottomed cards on the bottom in their original order; look-at-top-N effects (Stock Up, Dig Through Time, Lim-Dûl's Vault's bottoming) put the rest on the bottom in library order. Ponder, Brainstorm's put-back and Lim-Dûl's Vault's final top-of-library order ARE real choices (successive `choose_card_from_library` / `choose_discard` picks).
Cube spells-B: card-flow / casting-substrate shortcuts — 2026-09-27, `feature/cube-spells-b`11. **Decision hooks are reused, not added:** Brainstorm's put-back uses `choose_discard`; Exhume / Flash / Through the Breach / look-at-top picks use `choose_card_from_library` (the existing zone-agnostic precedent); Council's Judgment's non-caster votes use `choose_sacrifice`; Demonic Consultation's name uses `choose_mode`; Phyrexian life payment, splice, buyback-style "may pay" riders use `choose_yes_no`.

5 EoE pay-life shocklands admitted as plain untapped dual lands — `enters_tapped` / `pay-2-life` replacement dropped on BOTH engines (round-60 phase 1; activated-mana-ability cross-engine divergence CLOSED round-62)**What the shortcut is**: the production-deck trajectory-parity loader now admits the 5 EoE pay-life shocklands — **Breeding Pool, Watery Grave, Stomping Ground, Godless Shrine, Sacred Foundry** — as plain untapped dual-mana lands (a `CardDef(card_type="Land", mana_produced=<sorted dual>)`, the exact shape the basic-land arm emits, minus the `"Basic"` supertype gate). The real Magic card carries the replacement "As this land enters, you may pay 2 life. If you don't, it enters tapped." The live `OracleParserCardSource` **never structures that replacement at all** — it flattens each shockland to `produces={c1,c2}` + `enters_tapped=False` + zero abilities (verified round-60 against the live parser). The CardDef bridge has no `enters_tapped` field and Rust's `register_printing` has no land tapped-entry path, so the rider is dropped a SECOND time symmetrically. Net: the shockland is modeled as a vanilla untapped dual on BOTH engines — no pay-life decision, no tapped-entry, ever.
5 EoE pay-life shocklands admitted as plain untapped dual lands — `enters_tapped` / `pay-2-life` replacement dropped on BOTH engines (round-60 phase 1; activated-mana-ability cross-engine divergence CLOSED round-62)**Why it's OK**: the drop is **symmetric** — the parser flattens the printing identically before either engine sees it, so Python and Rust materialize the *same* untapped dual and round-trip **byte-equal**. Pinned at two levels: (1) static — 3 cross-engine bridge pins build the real Stomping Ground / Watery Grave / Breeding Pool CardDefs and assert `compare_fields() == []`; (2) **activated** (round-62 N1, the level round-61 N3 showed was missing) — an activated-mana-ability cross-engine pin drives `activate_ability` for EACH color index of all 5 real shocklands on BOTH engines and asserts a byte-equal pool (see the ✅ CLOSED round-62 block below); plus 1 genuine real-EoE probe drives real 17lands archetype 30 (Stomping Ground + Watery Grave) through `attack_all` divergence-free. The bench's `attack_all` strategy never makes the pay-life choice and never reads a land's tapped-state for a decision, so the *replacement* simplification is inert under the coverage it unlocks. This is the **round-39 Ward precedent** exactly (`CardDef bridge filter drops creatures with dynamic_pt_formula / ward_cost`, this doc above): a rider the bridge drops symmetrically, bit-equal under the bench play strategy, shipped blocked-at-fidelity rather than as a latent inter-engine divergence. (The activated-mana-ability path itself was a real latent divergence until round-62 fixed it — see the CLOSED block below.)
5 EoE pay-life shocklands admitted as plain untapped dual lands — `enters_tapped` / `pay-2-life` replacement dropped on BOTH engines (round-60 phase 1; activated-mana-ability cross-engine divergence CLOSED round-62)**Impact estimate**: **+5 cards / +18,065 cumulative 17lands decks** (Breeding Pool 4,712 + Watery Grave 4,226 + Stomping Ground 3,859 + Godless Shrine 2,937 + Sacred Foundry 2,331) unblocked into the production-deck bench, **0 strength cost** (no engine behavior changes; this is a bench-coverage admit, not a rules change). This is the entire *clean* realizable yield of the non-basic-land lever; the roadmap's remaining ~16,510-deck tail (the other 18) is gated behind the deferred Station / activated-ability / static / clone subsystems, not behind this substrate.

Engine code: `src/mtg_bot/effects/generic/cube_glue.py`, `src/mtg_bot/player_protections.py`, `src/mtg_bot/cube_glue_statics.py`, hooks in `turn.py` / `simulate.py` / `search/engine_adapter.py` (step hooks only) / `actions.py` / `legal.py` / `game.py`; grammar: `src/mtg_bot/cards/parser/cube_glue_grammar.py` (last `_parse_effect` fallback, switched off for EoE-only printings through the shared `creature_rmc_grammar` guard). Main-phase trigger points and delayed "your next main phase" triggers**Where:** `turn.run_beginning_of_precombat_main_triggers` (new `Event.BEGINNING_OF_PRECOMBAT_MAIN`), `turn.run_delayed_main_phase_triggers`; called from `simulate.run_step` and `search/engine_adapter._enter_step`. **What:** Coalition Relic's "your first main phase" is the precombat main phase; Mana Drain's delayed trigger (`delayed_triggers` entry, `"step": "main"`) fires at the controller's next main phase (the same turn's second main phase if the counter resolved before it, else their next turn's first). The Saga lore counter (layouts bucket) now rides the same hook. Mana added there floats until cleanup (the engine's pre-existing pool model). Mana Drain's amount is the countered spell's mana value as it last existed on the stack (X included); if the spell wasn't countered, nothing is scheduled. **Failure mode:** none known; the delayed trigger is an ordinary stack object. **Impact:** zero cost when no such trigger exists (one empty dispatch per main phase).

Rust port — Consult the Star Charts: kicker mana-payment cast pipeline NOW WIRED; probe drives a REAL Rust kicked cast (2026-06-01)1. ~~**Kicker mana-payment cast pipeline is NOT ported to Rust.**~~ **CLOSED (2026-06-01).** Consult the Star Charts carries the Kicker additional-cost mechanic (`kicker_cost = {1}{U}`). Python models kicker end-to-end (the `CastSpell.kicked` flag, `legal.py`'s kicked/unkicked dual emission, the base+kicker mana payment at `actions.py:1588-1601`, the `StackItem.kicked` field, the `state.resolving_kicked` swap). Rust now mirrors the cast side: `CardPrinting.kicker_cost: Option<ManaCost>` carries the kicker; `cast_spell_noncreature(obj_id, player_id, kicked=false)` (pyo3 optional arg — every pre-slice 2-arg caller stays byte-identical) folds the kicker onto the base cost (CR 601.2f total cost — generic + each colored pip summed, `x_pips` preserved) BEFORE X resolution, pays the combined cost via the SAME `auto_tap_pay_for_cost`, and mints `StackItem.was_kicked = true`. The `Action::CastSpell{kicked}` dispatch threads the flag through. A kicked cast with only base-mana available now correctly FAILS to pay (the kicker is genuinely charged, not a synthetic flag). Kicker on the CREATURE cast path (`cast_creature`) is still deferred (no kicker-carrying creature in the live EoE pool); warp/impending/free-cast cast-payment stay deferred under their own contracts (see the alt-cost map below).

Cube planeswalker bucket — engine shortcuts behind the claimed walkers (2026-09-27, `feature/cube-planeswalkers`)Claimed walkers: The Wandering Emperor, Elspeth Storm Slayer, Jace Wielder of Mysteries, Narset Parter of Veils, Teferi Time Raveler, Minsc & Boo, Saheeli Sublime Artificer, Jace the Mind Sculptor, Teferi Hero of Dominaria, Dack Fayden, Karn Scion of Urza (plus Tezzeret, Cruel Captain, unchanged). Each shortcut below is deliberate; none drops a printed clause.
Cube planeswalker bucket — engine shortcuts behind the claimed walkers (2026-09-27, `feature/cube-planeswalkers`)**8. Indefinite control changes set `controller_id` directly; the tuck bypasses `move_off_battlefield`.** *Where:* `cube_walkers.py::GainControlOfTargetPermanently` / `GainControlOfTriggeringSpellTargets` (Dack Fayden) follow `GainControlOfTargetSliverPermanently`'s precedent (no layer-2 registry entry; a later UEOT steal's cleanup revert can snap control back to its captured baseline). `PutTargetIntoOwnersLibraryNthFromTop` (Teferi, Hero of Dominaria's -3) leaves the battlefield the way `_bounce_to_hand` does — no leaves-the-battlefield triggers fire for the tucked permanent. *Fix scope:* route both through the registry / `move_off_battlefield` with a library destination, ~half a cycle.
Exchange of control and "they control" readings**Where:** `ExchangeControlOfTargets` (Oko's -5), `RevealHandMayExileCardOrChosenCreatureUntilSourceLeaves` (Cloak and Dagger). **What:** the exchange sets `controller_id` directly (the Dack Fayden precedent, no layer-2 entry); Cloak and Dagger's "creature they control" is "creature an opponent controls" (two players) and the choice between a hand card and the chosen creature goes through the generic `choose_card_from_library` id picker after a `choose_yes_no`.

Documented shortcuts (docs/SEARCH_LIMITATIONS.md)

Printed alternative costs share the `cast_for_free` action variant**What the shortcut is.** CR 118.9 alternative costs (Force of Will, Daze, Force of Negation / Vigor, Snuff Out, Mine Collapse, Baleful Mastery, Overload on Damn / Winds of Abandon) ride the casting substrate's existing `CastSpell(cast_for_free=True)` variant — the same one `alt_casting`'s pitch costs and conditional free casts use — so there is ONE cast-time alternative-cost path and the action encoding is unchanged (the codec already has a `cast_for_free` slot). The variant means "cast for an alternative cost" rather than naming WHICH one: a free-cast permission wins, and when a card prints several payable alternatives the caster's agent picks among them with `choose_mode` inside the cast. No printed card in either pool has two payable alternatives at once, so today the variant is unambiguous. Two further approximations: (1) `search/_player_capabilities.py`'s priority short-circuit only checks mana costs, so with that heuristic enabled a player whose only castable card is a free-cast (e.g. Force of Will with no untapped lands) can be skipped; (2) when several candidates can pay an alternative cost the pick reuses existing hooks: `choose_discard` for the exiled hand card (as `alt_casting.pay_pitch_cost` does), `choose_sacrifice` for the returned / sacrificed permanent.
Overload cast needs the single-target version's target**What the shortcut is.** An Overload cast (Damn, Winds of Abandon) is only offered when the non-overloaded "target" version has a legal target, so overloading onto a board with no legal target for the single-target version isn't offered. Such a cast would do nothing, so no strategic option is lost.

Documented shortcuts (docs/SEARCH_LIMITATIONS.md)

Subtlety removes a spell from mid-stack by index; Deep-Cavern Bat's hand exile**What the shortcut is.** Stack targets are `("stack", index)` pairs, so when Subtlety pulls a spell out from under other stack items, the engine re-indexes those items' `targets` above the removed spell; nothing else stores stack indices today, but a future effect that does would need the same fix-up. The owner's top/bottom choice goes through `choose_yes_no`. Deep-Cavern Bat's pick goes through `choose_card_from_opponent_hand`, and the card returns to its owner's hand (not the battlefield) through the base's until-leaves release hook.

Documented shortcuts (docs/SEARCH_LIMITATIONS.md)

Cube spells-B: card-flow / casting-substrate shortcuts — 2026-09-27, `feature/cube-spells-b`9. **Demonic Consultation's name choice** is one of the distinct names in the caster's library, or one "name not in your library" option (which exiles the whole library) — naming a specific card that isn't in the library is equivalent.
Cube spells-B: card-flow / casting-substrate shortcuts — 2026-09-27, `feature/cube-spells-b`11. **Decision hooks are reused, not added:** Brainstorm's put-back uses `choose_discard`; Exhume / Flash / Through the Breach / look-at-top picks use `choose_card_from_library` (the existing zone-agnostic precedent); Council's Judgment's non-caster votes use `choose_sacrifice`; Demonic Consultation's name uses `choose_mode`; Phyrexian life payment, splice, buyback-style "may pay" riders use `choose_yes_no`.
Other resolution-time choicesUgin's -11 and Nissa's -8 "any number" searches pick one card at a time through `choose_card_from_library` until the agent returns `None` (random / default agents take everything); Tamiyo's +1 names one of the distinct nonland names in your library or a "not in your library" option (the Demonic Consultation convention); Comet's "return a card with mana value 2 or less" (untargeted) uses the same id picker. Chandra's +1 casts through `cast_now` (the spell goes above the ability; if it's a land, uncastable, or declined, 2 damage to each opponent) and an uncast card stays in exile with no permission. Tidehollow Sculler follows the printed two-trigger text: if it leaves before its ETB resolves, the card is exiled forever.

Documented shortcuts (docs/SEARCH_LIMITATIONS.md)

The prepare-spell copy is a spell-copy object with a fixed caster**What the shortcut is.** The copy of the prepare spell is an exiled `GameObject` flagged `is_spell_copy` (so it ceases to exist when it leaves the stack) carrying a never-expiring `ExilePlayPermission` for the creature's controller *at the time it became prepared*; if control of the prepared creature changes, the permission doesn't follow the new controller (the rulings say only the current controller may cast it). "Becomes unprepared" effects other than casting the copy or the creature leaving the battlefield aren't modeled (no card in the pool prints one). The "if you control eight or more lands" gate of Emeritus of Abundance is checked when the ability triggers, not again on resolution (the parser's existing intervening-if convention).
The prepare-spell copy is a spell-copy object with a fixed caster**Impact.** Tiny (Emeritus of Abundance only).

PowerLSV cube W/G creature bucket — deliberate simplifications (2026-09-27, `feature/cube-creatures-wg`)5. **Batched "one or more ... enter" trigger** (Enduring Innocence) is the per-object ENTERS trigger with `once_per_turn`; the recognizer only accepts the form with "This ability triggers only once each turn.", where the two are equivalent.
PowerLSV cube "glue" bucket — deliberate simplifications (2026-09-27, `feature/cube-glue`)The last sixteen normal-layout cube cards (Chandra, Torch of Defiance; Oko, Thief of Crowns; Wrenn and Six; Ugin, Eye of the Storms; Kaito, Bane of Nightmares; Nissa, Who Shakes the World; Tamiyo, Collector of Tales; Comet, Stellar Pup; Shelldock Isle; Coalition Relic; Mana Drain; Fear of Missing Out; Mawloc; Cloak and Dagger, Entwined; Tidehollow Sculler; Gleemox). Engine code: `src/mtg_bot/effects/generic/cube_glue.py`, `src/mtg_bot/player_protections.py`, `src/mtg_bot/cube_glue_statics.py`, hooks in `turn.py` / `simulate.py` / `search/engine_adapter.py` (step hooks only) / `actions.py` / `legal.py` / `game.py`; grammar: `src/mtg_bot/cards/parser/cube_glue_grammar.py` (last `_parse_effect` fallback, switched off for EoE-only printings through the shared `creature_rmc_grammar` guard). Kaito, Bane of Nightmares and Fear of Missing Out are also Duskmourn printings, so -- like Enduring Innocence in the W/G bucket -- they become claimed in the `eoe` / `all` pools too; no other EoE printing's parse changes.

Documented shortcuts (docs/SEARCH_LIMITATIONS.md)

PowerLSV cube W/G creature bucket — deliberate simplifications (2026-09-27, `feature/cube-creatures-wg`)18. **Eternalize** (Fanatic of Rhonas; `creature_wg_lines._parse_eternalize_line`, `cube_creatures_wg.eternalized_printing`) is a graveyard-activated ability on the R/multi/colorless bucket's `graveyard_activated_abilities` substrate. The token is built from the card's printed characteristics at resolution (its copiable values; nothing modifies a card in exile) and keeps the Eternalize ability, which is inert on a token. Kicker on a creature (Sowing Mycospawn, `_parse_kicker_line`) reuses the spell kicker pipeline; its `{C}` pip is paid as generic (the engine-wide `parse_mana_cost` treatment of `{C}`).
PowerLSV cube W/G creature bucket — deliberate simplifications (2026-09-27, `feature/cube-creatures-wg`)21. **Targeted spells and "becomes the target"** (Surrak, Elusive Hunter): `cube_creatures_rmc.fire_becomes_target` now also dispatches `BECOMES_TARGET` for a spell targeted on the stack, with the spell as the `target_spell` subject (not `target`), so the existing "a permanent you control becomes the target" observers never see spells. The "Activate only if you control a creature with power N or greater" rider (Fanatic of Rhonas) is a `legal_actions` gate (`ActivationCost.requires_own_creature_power_at_least`), like the utility lands that already carry it.

Aura `flash` cast-timing rider dropped symmetrically (Aura-attachment Phase 2 first deliverable, round-79)**What the shortcut is**: the production-deck trajectory-parity loader now admits the two live EoE S1 Auras — **Frantic Strength** and **Shardmage's Rescue** — through the new `_printing_is_bridge_simple_aura` predicate (Phase-1 STEP-7 wire-up) even though both carry the `flash` cast-timing keyword (CR 702.8) on the source printing. `flash` is NOT in `_SAFE_KEYWORDS` (the creature-keyword admit set) and is documented as a known cross- engine divergence on creature CastSpell emission at instant-speed windows (see `parity/cross_engine.py` CE19 Bear-Flash probe — Python's `legal.py:217-301` emits CastSpell for `is_instant or "flash" in keywords`; Rust's `state_ops_legal.rs:759-764` short- circuits CastSpell on `active_player == player_id && phase in MAIN && stack.is_empty()` and never reads the flash keyword). For Auras specifically, the divergence is **bridged away** by the CardDef bridge's aura arm in `_printing_to_card_def` — the source's `keywords` field is NOT propagated through to the CardDef, so both Python's `_card_def_to_python_printing` and Rust's parse arm materialize the Aura with empty `keywords`. The `flash` rider is **symmetrically dropped** on BOTH bridge sides bit-equally before either engine sees the Aura.

Documented shortcuts (docs/SEARCH_LIMITATIONS.md)

Countered-spell destination is not part of the search hash**What the shortcut is.** Memory Lapse / Remand / Force of Negation / No More Lies record where the countered card goes on the `StackItem`; the search-side canonical-state hash (`search/canonical_state.py`, `search/info_set.py`) hashes `countered` but not the new destination field (search code is out of scope for the card campaign). Two states that differ only in whether a countered spell will go to the graveyard or back to its owner's hand collide in the transposition cache until the item is popped (one priority pass later).
Printed alternative costs share the `cast_for_free` action variant**What the shortcut is.** CR 118.9 alternative costs (Force of Will, Daze, Force of Negation / Vigor, Snuff Out, Mine Collapse, Baleful Mastery, Overload on Damn / Winds of Abandon) ride the casting substrate's existing `CastSpell(cast_for_free=True)` variant — the same one `alt_casting`'s pitch costs and conditional free casts use — so there is ONE cast-time alternative-cost path and the action encoding is unchanged (the codec already has a `cast_for_free` slot). The variant means "cast for an alternative cost" rather than naming WHICH one: a free-cast permission wins, and when a card prints several payable alternatives the caster's agent picks among them with `choose_mode` inside the cast. No printed card in either pool has two payable alternatives at once, so today the variant is unambiguous. Two further approximations: (1) `search/_player_capabilities.py`'s priority short-circuit only checks mana costs, so with that heuristic enabled a player whose only castable card is a free-cast (e.g. Force of Will with no untapped lands) can be skipped; (2) when several candidates can pay an alternative cost the pick reuses existing hooks: `choose_discard` for the exiled hand card (as `alt_casting.pay_pitch_cost` does), `choose_sacrifice` for the returned / sacrificed permanent.

Printed alternative costs share the `cast_for_free` action variant**What the shortcut is.** CR 118.9 alternative costs (Force of Will, Daze, Force of Negation / Vigor, Snuff Out, Mine Collapse, Baleful Mastery, Overload on Damn / Winds of Abandon) ride the casting substrate's existing `CastSpell(cast_for_free=True)` variant — the same one `alt_casting`'s pitch costs and conditional free casts use — so there is ONE cast-time alternative-cost path and the action encoding is unchanged (the codec already has a `cast_for_free` slot). The variant means "cast for an alternative cost" rather than naming WHICH one: a free-cast permission wins, and when a card prints several payable alternatives the caster's agent picks among them with `choose_mode` inside the cast. No printed card in either pool has two payable alternatives at once, so today the variant is unambiguous. Two further approximations: (1) `search/_player_capabilities.py`'s priority short-circuit only checks mana costs, so with that heuristic enabled a player whose only castable card is a free-cast (e.g. Force of Will with no untapped lands) can be skipped; (2) when several candidates can pay an alternative cost the pick reuses existing hooks: `choose_discard` for the exiled hand card (as `alt_casting.pay_pitch_cost` does), `choose_sacrifice` for the returned / sacrificed permanent.

Loader-admit gate is a reduced-card-universe boundary (DOCUMENTED + ENFORCEABLE — C6 pin landed)**What the shortcut is.** The parity loader admits a card-name only if it passes one of 5 bridge-support disjuncts (`basic_land`, `nonbasic_mana_land`, `pure_warp_creature`, `simple_creature`, `simple_spell`); any other name is dropped and the deck is Forest-padded to size. Per `docs/LOADER_ADMIT_COMPLETENESS_ANALYSIS.md` (re-measured `4704ca3e`): pool admit 10.95%, mean non-land deck-slot admit ~19.7%, **0 / 129,996 real decks fully admittable**. The bench therefore plays the *admitted residue of real decks, Forest-padded* — a deliberately reduced card universe.
Loader-admit gate is a reduced-card-universe boundary (DOCUMENTED + ENFORCEABLE — C6 pin landed)**Why it's OK.** This is the accepted staged-flip fence (`docs/SOT_FLIP_CUTOVER_PLAN.md` C5/C6/§7-OQ3). While Python is the source of truth (single-script-replay), the silent drop is benign: both engines replay the SAME action-dict, so a Forest-padded reduced deck is still a faithful cross-engine parity probe. The byte-equal campaign metric is honest *over the admitted population*, which is exactly what the bench exercises.
Loader-admit gate is a reduced-card-universe boundary (DOCUMENTED + ENFORCEABLE — C6 pin landed)**Failure mode (and the C6 closure).** At/after the SoT flip the silent drop would become a *silent correctness hole* — a Rust-sourced bot would quietly play a different (reduced, Forest-padded) deck than intended, with no signal. C6 closes this: the boundary is now **observable** (`LoaderAdmitReport` names every dropped slot + Forest-pad count, with multiplicity) and **fail-loud-enforceable** (`LoaderAdmitPolicy.RAISE` raises `NonAdmittedCardError` instead of silently degrading — the post-flip Rust-sourced path sets this). The default `production_deck_to_deckspec` path is **bit-identical** to the pre-C6 behavior (parity-neutral; the silent drop stays the Python-SoT default). **Pinned by:** `tests/test_c6_loader_admit_boundary.py` (observable not silent, fail-loud RAISE, parity-neutral default-path-bit-identical).

Aura `flash` cast-timing rider dropped symmetrically (Aura-attachment Phase 2 first deliverable, round-79)**Why it's OK**: the drop is **symmetric** — the CardDef bridge flattens the Aura's `keywords` to the empty frozenset identically on both engines, so Python and Rust each materialize the SAME ``keywords=frozenset()`` printing and round-trip byte-equal on every aura field that DOES round-trip (`is_aura`, `aura_enchant_type`, `aura_yours_only`, `equipment_bonuses`). Pinned at three levels: (1) static — Phase 2 first-deliverable tests (`tests/test_aura_substrate_phase_2.py`, `test_carddef_bridge_drops_flash_symmetrically_for_*`) assert the post-bridge `keywords == frozenset()` on both engines for each S1 carrier; (2) loader — `test_loader_admits_real_eoe_frantic_strength_deck` drives a mixed Forest + bridge-simple-creature + Frantic Strength deck through `_filter_deck_to_bridge_supported` divergence-free; (3) cross-engine — `test_phase_2_aura_decks_pec_round_trips_python_rust` builds the SAME DeckSpec on both engines and asserts the aura fields read back identically from Rust's registry via `read_rust_printing_aura_fields`. The bench's `attack_all` strategy only ever casts at sorcery speed where the `flash`-gate fork is irrelevant on BOTH engines (Rust's sorcery-timing predicate covers every non-instant spell; Python's instant-speed block is gated on `is_instant or "flash"` and runs at sorcery windows anyway via the falling-through sorcery emit). This is the **round-39 Ward / round-59 shockland precedent** exactly: a rider the bridge drops symmetrically, bit-equal under the bench play strategy, shipped blocked-at-fidelity rather than as a latent inter-engine divergence.

Nissa's extra mana rides automatic payment only**Where:** `actions.extra_mana_grants_for_tapped_lands`, `_can_pay_from` / `_virtual_pretap` in `can_pay_cost`, `_pretap_lands_for_extra_mana` in `auto_tap_for_cost`. **What:** "Whenever you tap a Forest for mana, add an additional {G}" is folded into the automatic payer: affordability tries pre-tapping 1..all Forests (fewest other colors first), and payment taps Forests into the pool first while the cost isn't otherwise payable, floating any surplus {G} for the rest of the turn. The Forest's own mana is taken as {G}. Phyrexian-split affordability doesn't know the bonus. **Failure mode:** a dual Forest may be pre-tapped for {G} when its other color was needed only if every alternative failed; surplus floating mana is spent later that turn or lost at cleanup. **Impact:** the extra check runs only when the normal affordability check fails and a grant exists (a battlefield scan).

Opening-hand actions are setup-agent decisions (2026-09-28, `feature/cube-fixes-1`)**Where:** `mtg_bot/opening_hand.py` (`apply_opening_hand_actions`), called from `simulate.setup_game` after the final keep; `CardPrinting.opening_hand_action` (parsed by `cards/parser/opening_hand_lines.py`). **What:** CR 103.6 opening-hand actions — Gemstone Caverns' "you may begin the game with it on the battlefield with a luck counter on it; if you do, exile a card from your hand" (non-starting player only) — are asked of the seat's *setup* agent through the generic `Agent.choose_yes_no` hook, with the exiled card picked through `choose_discard`. In self-play / data-gen the setup agents are `RandomAgent`s (a coin flip and a random exile), `DefaultTacticalAgent` always says yes and exiles the first card; search / the NN never see the decision (it happens before the first searched state, like the mulligan). **Why OK:** it is one binary pre-game choice on one cube card, and "yes" is almost always right. **Failure mode:** a self-play seat declines a free accelerant half the time; the policy cannot learn the choice. **Fix scope:** a pre-game decision node in the search adapter (shared with mulligans). **Impact:** small, one card. Callers that alternate the starting seat must pass `setup_game(..., starting_player_idx=...)` (data-gen now does) — patching `active_player_idx` afterwards would offer Gemstone Caverns to the wrong player. Leyline of Mutation (EoE-era pool) prints the bare form of the same line and still takes the enchantment builder's honest-no-op path; routing it through `parse_opening_hand_line` is a one-line change deferred so that pool's parses don't move in this branch. The Rust engine has no opening-hand hook, no `produces_with_counter` and no `SourceHasCounter`; Gemstone Caverns no longer matches its parity-probe shape (`AddManaToPool(any)`).

PowerLSV cube "glue" bucket — deliberate simplifications (2026-09-27, `feature/cube-glue`)The last sixteen normal-layout cube cards (Chandra, Torch of Defiance; Oko, Thief of Crowns; Wrenn and Six; Ugin, Eye of the Storms; Kaito, Bane of Nightmares; Nissa, Who Shakes the World; Tamiyo, Collector of Tales; Comet, Stellar Pup; Shelldock Isle; Coalition Relic; Mana Drain; Fear of Missing Out; Mawloc; Cloak and Dagger, Entwined; Tidehollow Sculler; Gleemox). Engine code: `src/mtg_bot/effects/generic/cube_glue.py`, `src/mtg_bot/player_protections.py`, `src/mtg_bot/cube_glue_statics.py`, hooks in `turn.py` / `simulate.py` / `search/engine_adapter.py` (step hooks only) / `actions.py` / `legal.py` / `game.py`; grammar: `src/mtg_bot/cards/parser/cube_glue_grammar.py` (last `_parse_effect` fallback, switched off for EoE-only printings through the shared `creature_rmc_grammar` guard). Kaito, Bane of Nightmares and Fear of Missing Out are also Duskmourn printings, so -- like Enduring Innocence in the W/G bucket -- they become claimed in the `eoe` / `all` pools too; no other EoE printing's parse changes.
"This card is banned." is a deck-construction statement**Where:** `printing_keywords._DECK_CONSTRUCTION_STATEMENT_LINE` (artifact builder). **What:** Gleemox's line (and the "A deck can have any number of / up to N cards named <this card>." family, CR 100.2a) only constrains deck building; the engine plays already-built decks, so the recognizer claims exactly that class of statement and records nothing -- the same treatment as "<name> can be your commander." **Failure mode:** none in play; a deck builder that consults the printing won't see the ban. **Fix scope:** a `CardPrinting.deck_construction` note if a deck builder ever needs it (~minutes).

5 EoE pay-life shocklands admitted as plain untapped dual lands — `enters_tapped` / `pay-2-life` replacement dropped on BOTH engines (round-60 phase 1; activated-mana-ability cross-engine divergence CLOSED round-62)**What the shortcut is**: the production-deck trajectory-parity loader now admits the 5 EoE pay-life shocklands — **Breeding Pool, Watery Grave, Stomping Ground, Godless Shrine, Sacred Foundry** — as plain untapped dual-mana lands (a `CardDef(card_type="Land", mana_produced=<sorted dual>)`, the exact shape the basic-land arm emits, minus the `"Basic"` supertype gate). The real Magic card carries the replacement "As this land enters, you may pay 2 life. If you don't, it enters tapped." The live `OracleParserCardSource` **never structures that replacement at all** — it flattens each shockland to `produces={c1,c2}` + `enters_tapped=False` + zero abilities (verified round-60 against the live parser). The CardDef bridge has no `enters_tapped` field and Rust's `register_printing` has no land tapped-entry path, so the rider is dropped a SECOND time symmetrically. Net: the shockland is modeled as a vanilla untapped dual on BOTH engines — no pay-life decision, no tapped-entry, ever.
5 EoE pay-life shocklands admitted as plain untapped dual lands — `enters_tapped` / `pay-2-life` replacement dropped on BOTH engines (round-60 phase 1; activated-mana-ability cross-engine divergence CLOSED round-62)**Impact estimate**: **+5 cards / +18,065 cumulative 17lands decks** (Breeding Pool 4,712 + Watery Grave 4,226 + Stomping Ground 3,859 + Godless Shrine 2,937 + Sacred Foundry 2,331) unblocked into the production-deck bench, **0 strength cost** (no engine behavior changes; this is a bench-coverage admit, not a rules change). This is the entire *clean* realizable yield of the non-basic-land lever; the roadmap's remaining ~16,510-deck tail (the other 18) is gated behind the deferred Station / activated-ability / static / clone subsystems, not behind this substrate.

Documented shortcuts (docs/SEARCH_LIMITATIONS.md)

PowerLSV cube creatures bucket (red / multicolor / colorless) — engine shortcuts (2026-09-27, `feature/cube-creatures-rmc`)1. **Exile play permissions** (`rmc.ExilePlayPermission`: Ragavan, Robber of the Rich, Laelia, Inti, Headliner Scarlett, ...). The permission rides the exiled card (`GameObject.exile_play_permission`), so it works from any player's exile zone; plays are offered by `legal._exile_permission_plays`. Expiry runs at the cleanup step (`rmc.expire_exile_play_permissions` from `turn.run_cleanup_step`), so an "until your next end step" card stays playable during that end step itself (CR ends it as the end step begins). The permission is cleared only when the card is played through it or expires, so a card that leaves exile some other way and is exiled again by an unrelated effect keeps a stale permission (CR 400.7 would make it a new object with none). The action codec has no slot for "cast a card from an opponent's exile", so those plays share the plain `CastSpell` variant, and `canonical_state` doesn't hash the permission. *Impact:* small — the permission is usually used or lost within a turn. *Fix scope:* hash the permission; add a codec slot.

Rust port — Consult the Star Charts: kicker mana-payment cast pipeline NOW WIRED; probe drives a REAL Rust kicked cast (2026-06-01)2. ~~**The probe drives the kicked branch via a synthetic StackItem setter, not a real kicked cast.**~~ **CLOSED (2026-06-01).** The cross-engine probe now drives a REAL kicked cast on both engines: Python's genuine `_cast_spell(..., kicked=True)` (folds kicker_cost, auto-taps blue Islands, sets `StackItem.kicked`) and Rust's real `cast_spell_noncreature(spell_id, 0, kicked=True)` (folds kicker_cost, pays base+kicker, mints `was_kicked`). The lands now produce blue mana (Island subtype + `mana_produced=["U"]`) so the {1}{U}{1}{U} combined cost is auto-tap-payable; X (= land count) tracks the funding land count, and the library staging is sized so the kept/bottomed sets match across both engines byte-equal. The `set_stack_top_was_ kicked` synthetic setter is retained as a low-level substrate (pinned by `test_rust_was_kicked_stack_flag_round_trips`) but is no longer the parity-load-bearing driver. The legal-action kicked/unkicked dual emission on the Rust legal-cast path was NOT needed for byte-equal parity here (the probe calls the cast primitive directly, mirroring every other cross-engine cast probe); Python's `legal.py` dual emission is the SoT and unchanged.
Converge counts the colors of the lands the auto-tapper happened to pick**What the shortcut is.** The count is the maximum number of distinct colors the mana actually spent could have produced (dual lands count as whichever color helps), but *which* lands are tapped is decided by `auto_tap_for_cost`'s greedy order, which doesn't try to diversify colors. With two Plains and an Island available, an X=1 Prismatic Ending may be paid with both Plains (1 color) even though Plains + Island (2 colors) was possible. Convoke-tapped creatures don't count toward converge.

Cube planeswalker bucket — engine shortcuts behind the claimed walkers (2026-09-27, `feature/cube-planeswalkers`)**7. Winning the game preempts a same-resolution empty-library draw.** *Where:* `turn.py::win_the_game`. The engine records "drew from an empty library" as an immediate loss in `draw_card`; the rules make it a state-based action (CR 704.5b). `win_the_game` therefore clears that pending flag for the winner (only that reason) — matching Jace, Wielder of Mysteries' -8 ("Draw seven cards. Then if your library has no cards in it, you win the game."), where the win happens before any SBA check.

Engine code: `src/mtg_bot/effects/generic/cube_glue.py`, `src/mtg_bot/player_protections.py`, `src/mtg_bot/cube_glue_statics.py`, hooks in `turn.py` / `simulate.py` / `search/engine_adapter.py` (step hooks only) / `actions.py` / `legal.py` / `game.py`; grammar: `src/mtg_bot/cards/parser/cube_glue_grammar.py` (last `_parse_effect` fallback, switched off for EoE-only printings through the shared `creature_rmc_grammar` guard). Kaito, Bane of Nightmares and Fear of Missing Out are also Duskmourn printings, so -- like Enduring Innocence in the W/G bucket -- they become claimed in the `eoe` / `all` pools too; no other EoE printing's parse changes.

Delirium and card-type counting (2026-09-28, `feature/cube-fixes-1`)Every "card types among cards in <zone>" count now goes through `mtg_bot.effects.card_types` (`card_types_of`, `count_card_types`, `delirium_active`): Delirium at both predicate tiers (`state_predicates.Delirium` for trigger gates, `conditions.DeliriumActive` for statics / "instead if" spell riders / activation restrictions — both carry the printed `min_card_types=4` and delegate to the one function), the Lhurgoyfs, Ursine Monstrosity, Keen-Eyed Curator, Occult Epiphany and Atraxa. What was wrong before: the delirium type set listed only the pre-2024 name "Tribal" (a Kindred card counted for nothing), each goyf / Ursine / Curator / Epiphany / Atraxa helper carried its own type tuple, and a card whose printing was still a back face / split half off the stack would have been read by that face. The shared helper folds Tribal into Kindred, unions a split card's halves (CR 709.4), reads a DFC by its front face (CR 712.8a — an MDFC land such as Shatterskull Smashing is a *sorcery* card in a graveyard, so it does NOT give delirium a land), reads an adventurer by its normal characteristics (CR 715.4) and skips tokens / spell copies (not cards).

Documented shortcuts (docs/SEARCH_LIMITATIONS.md)

Cube spells-B: card-flow / casting-substrate shortcuts — 2026-09-27, `feature/cube-spells-b`1. **"In any order" orderings are not offered.** Scry (`bottom_choice=True`) keeps the kept cards on top and the bottomed cards on the bottom in their original order; look-at-top-N effects (Stock Up, Dig Through Time, Lim-Dûl's Vault's bottoming) put the rest on the bottom in library order. Ponder, Brainstorm's put-back and Lim-Dûl's Vault's final top-of-library order ARE real choices (successive `choose_card_from_library` / `choose_discard` picks).
Cube spells-B: card-flow / casting-substrate shortcuts — 2026-09-27, `feature/cube-spells-b`8. **Lim-Dûl's Vault's repeat loop stops** once another payment would drop the caster to 0 life or every card of the library has been seen.

Documented shortcuts (docs/SEARCH_LIMITATIONS.md)

PowerLSV cube "glue" bucket — deliberate simplifications (2026-09-27, `feature/cube-glue`)The last sixteen normal-layout cube cards (Chandra, Torch of Defiance; Oko, Thief of Crowns; Wrenn and Six; Ugin, Eye of the Storms; Kaito, Bane of Nightmares; Nissa, Who Shakes the World; Tamiyo, Collector of Tales; Comet, Stellar Pup; Shelldock Isle; Coalition Relic; Mana Drain; Fear of Missing Out; Mawloc; Cloak and Dagger, Entwined; Tidehollow Sculler; Gleemox). Engine code: `src/mtg_bot/effects/generic/cube_glue.py`, `src/mtg_bot/player_protections.py`, `src/mtg_bot/cube_glue_statics.py`, hooks in `turn.py` / `simulate.py` / `search/engine_adapter.py` (step hooks only) / `actions.py` / `legal.py` / `game.py`; grammar: `src/mtg_bot/cards/parser/cube_glue_grammar.py` (last `_parse_effect` fallback, switched off for EoE-only printings through the shared `creature_rmc_grammar` guard). Kaito, Bane of Nightmares and Fear of Missing Out are also Duskmourn printings, so -- like Enduring Innocence in the W/G bucket -- they become claimed in the `eoe` / `all` pools too; no other EoE printing's parse changes.
Main-phase trigger points and delayed "your next main phase" triggers**Where:** `turn.run_beginning_of_precombat_main_triggers` (new `Event.BEGINNING_OF_PRECOMBAT_MAIN`), `turn.run_delayed_main_phase_triggers`; called from `simulate.run_step` and `search/engine_adapter._enter_step`. **What:** Coalition Relic's "your first main phase" is the precombat main phase; Mana Drain's delayed trigger (`delayed_triggers` entry, `"step": "main"`) fires at the controller's next main phase (the same turn's second main phase if the counter resolved before it, else their next turn's first). The Saga lore counter (layouts bucket) now rides the same hook. Mana added there floats until cleanup (the engine's pre-existing pool model). Mana Drain's amount is the countered spell's mana value as it last existed on the stack (X included); if the spell wasn't countered, nothing is scheduled. **Failure mode:** none known; the delayed trigger is an ordinary stack object. **Impact:** zero cost when no such trigger exists (one empty dispatch per main phase).

Documented shortcuts (docs/SEARCH_LIMITATIONS.md)

Rust-parity-pinned lossy legacy spells**What the shortcut is.** The compositional phrase grammar models "target creature or planeswalker", "counter target spell unless its controller pays {N}", and other surfaces faithfully, but five Edge-of-Eternities-era spells were claimed earlier through lossy legacy recognizers (planeswalker target arm dropped, pay-or-counter tax dropped, riders dropped, or only one of several modes kept) and their simplified models are pinned by cross-engine parity tests against the Rust engine: Divert Disaster, Don't Make a Sound, Archenemy's Charm, Scorching Dragonfire, Break Down the Door (plus Get Out / Untimely Malfunction for the single-parseable-mode modal fallback). While one of those names is being parsed the compositional grammar is switched off, so they keep the legacy models. Every other card with the same printed surfaces (including the cube's Mana Leak, Sear, Baleful Mastery, Unholy Heat, Mine Collapse, …) now parses faithfully, and the single-parseable-mode fallback no longer claims non-legacy modal spells (Suplex, Sheoldred's Edict must parse every mode).

Tamiyo's protection is checked at the discard / sacrifice sites**Where:** `player_protections.opponent_effect_blocked_for`, `GameState.resolving_item_controller_id` (set by `actions.resolve_top_of_stack`), consulted by `turn.sacrifice` and the effect-driven discard sites (`card_flow.discard_card`, the discard effect classes, `life.py`, the Fanatic / Memory Jar / cube R-multi hand discards). **What:** a discard or sacrifice that happens while an opponent-controlled spell/ability resolves is skipped. Costs are paid by their own controller outside the opponent's resolution, so they're never blocked. Osseous Sticktwister's "sacrifice or discard or take damage" choice (an EoE punisher) still offers the blocked options; choosing one does nothing (and avoids the damage). A discard site added later that bypasses these helpers would ignore the protection. **Fix scope:** a single discard choke point (see the U/B section's graveyard choke-point note).

Documented shortcuts (docs/SEARCH_LIMITATIONS.md)

Rust-parity-pinned lossy legacy spells**What the shortcut is.** The compositional phrase grammar models "target creature or planeswalker", "counter target spell unless its controller pays {N}", and other surfaces faithfully, but five Edge-of-Eternities-era spells were claimed earlier through lossy legacy recognizers (planeswalker target arm dropped, pay-or-counter tax dropped, riders dropped, or only one of several modes kept) and their simplified models are pinned by cross-engine parity tests against the Rust engine: Divert Disaster, Don't Make a Sound, Archenemy's Charm, Scorching Dragonfire, Break Down the Door (plus Get Out / Untimely Malfunction for the single-parseable-mode modal fallback). While one of those names is being parsed the compositional grammar is switched off, so they keep the legacy models. Every other card with the same printed surfaces (including the cube's Mana Leak, Sear, Baleful Mastery, Unholy Heat, Mine Collapse, …) now parses faithfully, and the single-parseable-mode fallback no longer claims non-legacy modal spells (Suplex, Sheoldred's Edict must parse every mode).
Printed alternative costs share the `cast_for_free` action variant**What the shortcut is.** CR 118.9 alternative costs (Force of Will, Daze, Force of Negation / Vigor, Snuff Out, Mine Collapse, Baleful Mastery, Overload on Damn / Winds of Abandon) ride the casting substrate's existing `CastSpell(cast_for_free=True)` variant — the same one `alt_casting`'s pitch costs and conditional free casts use — so there is ONE cast-time alternative-cost path and the action encoding is unchanged (the codec already has a `cast_for_free` slot). The variant means "cast for an alternative cost" rather than naming WHICH one: a free-cast permission wins, and when a card prints several payable alternatives the caster's agent picks among them with `choose_mode` inside the cast. No printed card in either pool has two payable alternatives at once, so today the variant is unambiguous. Two further approximations: (1) `search/_player_capabilities.py`'s priority short-circuit only checks mana costs, so with that heuristic enabled a player whose only castable card is a free-cast (e.g. Force of Will with no untapped lands) can be skipped; (2) when several candidates can pay an alternative cost the pick reuses existing hooks: `choose_discard` for the exiled hand card (as `alt_casting.pay_pitch_cost` does), `choose_sacrifice` for the returned / sacrificed permanent.

Cube lands (line-composed land grammar): automatic mana payment, hand abilities, life-costed taps — 2026-09-27, `feature/cube-lands`1. **Automatic payment only uses a land's `produces` set.** Lands built by the line-composed grammar set `mana_only_from_produces=True`: a land contributes to `can_pay_cost` / `auto_tap_for_cost` only through its free (or life-costed) `{T}: Add` production. Mana abilities with any other cost or shape — Gaea's Cradle / Tolarian Academy (scaling), Mishra's Workshop (spend restriction), Sunken Ruins (filter, `{U/B}` input), Gemstone Mine (counter cost), Starting Town's `{T}, Pay 1 life: Add one mana of any color`, Arena of Glory's exert ability — are explicit mana abilities, usable only by activating them (which `legal_actions` offers only in a sorcery window, like every activated ability) and floating the mana. So none of them can pay for an instant-speed cast.

PowerLSV cube enchantment bucket — deliberate simplifications (2026-09-27, `feature/cube-enchantments`)1. **Necromancy's "as though it had flash" is the `flash` keyword** on the printing. The only observable difference (a permanent "having flash") isn't read by anything in the pool.
PowerLSV cube enchantment bucket — deliberate simplifications (2026-09-27, `feature/cube-enchantments`)2. **Cleanup-step delayed triggers resolve without priority** (`enchantment_mechanics.run_delayed_cleanup_triggers`, called at the end of `turn.run_cleanup_step`). Necromancy cast when a sorcery couldn't have been is sacrificed at the next cleanup step; its leaves trigger (and any other trigger that sacrifice causes) is resolved immediately in stack order and SBAs are checked. CR 514.3a would give players priority and run another cleanup step, so no one can respond to those triggers. *Impact:* negligible (responses to "sacrifice that creature" are rare).

Documented shortcuts (docs/SEARCH_LIMITATIONS.md)

Countered-spell destination is not part of the search hash**What the shortcut is.** Memory Lapse / Remand / Force of Negation / No More Lies record where the countered card goes on the `StackItem`; the search-side canonical-state hash (`search/canonical_state.py`, `search/info_set.py`) hashes `countered` but not the new destination field (search code is out of scope for the card campaign). Two states that differ only in whether a countered spell will go to the graveyard or back to its owner's hand collide in the transposition cache until the item is popped (one priority pass later).

PowerLSV cube enchantment bucket — deliberate simplifications (2026-09-27, `feature/cube-enchantments`)4. **Oath of Druids' target is picked by the Oath controller's agent**, not by "that player" (the upkeep's active player). The legal set (opponents of the active player with more creatures) has at most one member in two-player games, so the choice is forced. If the revealed cards contain no creature card, nothing moves (the revealed library stays in order) — the "If the first player does" clause fails.

Documented shortcuts (docs/SEARCH_LIMITATIONS.md)

Delirium and card-type counting (2026-09-28, `feature/cube-fixes-1`)Every "card types among cards in <zone>" count now goes through `mtg_bot.effects.card_types` (`card_types_of`, `count_card_types`, `delirium_active`): Delirium at both predicate tiers (`state_predicates.Delirium` for trigger gates, `conditions.DeliriumActive` for statics / "instead if" spell riders / activation restrictions — both carry the printed `min_card_types=4` and delegate to the one function), the Lhurgoyfs, Ursine Monstrosity, Keen-Eyed Curator, Occult Epiphany and Atraxa. What was wrong before: the delirium type set listed only the pre-2024 name "Tribal" (a Kindred card counted for nothing), each goyf / Ursine / Curator / Epiphany / Atraxa helper carried its own type tuple, and a card whose printing was still a back face / split half off the stack would have been read by that face. The shared helper folds Tribal into Kindred, unions a split card's halves (CR 709.4), reads a DFC by its front face (CR 712.8a — an MDFC land such as Shatterskull Smashing is a *sorcery* card in a graveyard, so it does NOT give delirium a land), reads an adventurer by its normal characteristics (CR 715.4) and skips tokens / spell copies (not cards).

Draw-step "first card" bookkeeping**What the shortcut is.** Only the draw performed by the turn-based action counts as "the first one they draw in each of their draw steps" (Orcish Bowmasters, Hullbreacher); if another effect replaced that draw (none in the pool can while the exemption applies), the next draw in the step would not be treated as the first. Per-card draw replacements apply once per card inside a multi-card draw (CR 121.6).

The trajectory safe-trigger admit gate (`parity/trajectory.py::_python_ta_to_safe_dict`) is INTENTIONALLY NOT widened — that gate is about the production-deck bench admit set, a distinct concern from per-card real-EoE parity probes. **The card DOES move to PROBED tier through the dedicated per-card real- EoE byte-equal cross-engine probe** (`tests/test_weftwalking_ parity.py`), the same precedent as Splitskin Doll / Boilerbilges Ripper / Possibility Technician / Friendly Teddy / Endstone / Terrapact / Vaultguard / Arabella / Attack-in-the-Box / Wickerfolk Thresher / Enduring Curiosity / Terrasymbiosis / Ouroboroid / Blade of the Swarm established.

No real-EoE source-power consumer (Infernal Phantom DIES, Rust Harvester AA, Ouroboroid beginning-of-combat trigger) stages an anthem/switch rider on the source, so this is observationally byte-equal on the genuine pool.
DealDamageEqualToSourcePowerAnyTarget — DIES-trigger LKI + counter read (CLOSED, hub todo ddc12150)**Sibling-pattern audit**: the two non-DSK source-power consumers are **Rust Harvester** (`DealDamageEqualToSourcePowerAnyTarget`, on-bf activated — had the latent counter bug, now byte-equal) and **Ouroboroid** (`PutPlusOneCountersOnEachCreatureYouControlEqualToSource Power`, on-bf beginning-of-combat trigger — uses `read_famished_source_power`, already counter-correct and not DIES- reachable, so unaffected). No other `*EqualToSourcePower*` Rust resolve arm has the battlefield-only-search shape that is DIES-reachable.

PowerLSV cube artifact bucket — deliberate simplifications (2026-09-27, `feature/cube-artifacts`)3. **Sunburst counts colors of the mana the auto-payer spent** (`auto_tap_for_cost(color_sources=…)` + `max_distinct_colors`). Documented shortcuts (docs/SEARCH_LIMITATIONS.md)

Improvise, Saddle and clones**What the shortcut is.** Improvise is checked like convoke (upper-bound affordability), and the engine -- not the agent -- picks which artifacts to tap: artifacts without mana abilities first, as many as the generic cost needs, before any land is tapped. Keeping an artifact untapped instead of a land is therefore not a searchable choice. Saddle picks riders one at a time through `choose_permanent_to_tap` (plain power; crew-only bonuses don't apply). Phyrexian Metamorph / Superior Spider-Man copy the target's printing (its copiable values); Superior Spider-Man's "When you do, exile that card." is a trigger put on the stack right after it enters.

Cube spells-B: card-flow / casting-substrate shortcuts — 2026-09-27, `feature/cube-spells-b`1. **"In any order" orderings are not offered.** Scry (`bottom_choice=True`) keeps the kept cards on top and the bottomed cards on the bottom in their original order; look-at-top-N effects (Stock Up, Dig Through Time, Lim-Dûl's Vault's bottoming) put the rest on the bottom in library order. Ponder, Brainstorm's put-back and Lim-Dûl's Vault's final top-of-library order ARE real choices (successive `choose_card_from_library` / `choose_discard` picks).
PowerLSV cube artifact bucket — deliberate simplifications (2026-09-27, `feature/cube-artifacts`)15. **Activated abilities whose effect is several sentences** (Wishclaw Talisman) fall back to a sentence-by-sentence parse in `activated.py` only after the whole-effect parse failed; spell text keeps the base compound grammar (so Ponder's nested shape is unchanged).

Converge counts the colors of the lands the auto-tapper happened to pick**What the shortcut is.** The count is the maximum number of distinct colors the mana actually spent could have produced (dual lands count as whichever color helps), but *which* lands are tapped is decided by `auto_tap_for_cost`'s greedy order, which doesn't try to diversify colors. With two Plains and an Island available, an X=1 Prismatic Ending may be paid with both Plains (1 color) even though Plains + Island (2 colors) was possible. Convoke-tapped creatures don't count toward converge.

PowerLSV cube creatures bucket (red / multicolor / colorless) — engine shortcuts (2026-09-27, `feature/cube-creatures-rmc`)6. **Non-combat damage from these effects carries no source.** Fights (`rmc.SourceFightsTarget`), Pyrogoyf-style event damage (`rmc.DealDamageFromEvent`) and Batroc's per-kick damage go through `effects.base._apply_damage`, which is source-agnostic, so the source's deathtouch / lifelink / infect don't apply. Power is read at resolution; when the source has left the battlefield, last-known power comes from `rmc.find_object_anywhere` (printed power + counters).

Documented shortcuts (docs/SEARCH_LIMITATIONS.md)

Countered-spell destination is not part of the search hash**What the shortcut is.** Memory Lapse / Remand / Force of Negation / No More Lies record where the countered card goes on the `StackItem`; the search-side canonical-state hash (`search/canonical_state.py`, `search/info_set.py`) hashes `countered` but not the new destination field (search code is out of scope for the card campaign). Two states that differ only in whether a countered spell will go to the graveyard or back to its owner's hand collide in the transposition cache until the item is popped (one priority pass later).
Spell-level fizzle for multi-effect spells**Where:** `effects/combinators.py::Sequence` (pre-existing engine behaviour, newly exercised by Remand).
Spell-level fizzle for multi-effect spells**What the shortcut is.** CR 608.2b says a spell whose every target has become illegal doesn't resolve at all. The engine re-checks legality per effect, so a `Sequence` like Remand ("Counter target spell. … Draw a card.") still draws a card when its target spell has already left the stack. Pre-existing for every multi-sentence targeted spell (Radiant Strike, …).

Documented shortcuts (docs/SEARCH_LIMITATIONS.md)

PowerLSV cube creatures bucket (red / multicolor / colorless) — engine shortcuts (2026-09-27, `feature/cube-creatures-rmc`)1. **Exile play permissions** (`rmc.ExilePlayPermission`: Ragavan, Robber of the Rich, Laelia, Inti, Headliner Scarlett, ...). The permission rides the exiled card (`GameObject.exile_play_permission`), so it works from any player's exile zone; plays are offered by `legal._exile_permission_plays`. Expiry runs at the cleanup step (`rmc.expire_exile_play_permissions` from `turn.run_cleanup_step`), so an "until your next end step" card stays playable during that end step itself (CR ends it as the end step begins). The permission is cleared only when the card is played through it or expires, so a card that leaves exile some other way and is exiled again by an unrelated effect keeps a stale permission (CR 400.7 would make it a new object with none). The action codec has no slot for "cast a card from an opponent's exile", so those plays share the plain `CastSpell` variant, and `canonical_state` doesn't hash the permission. *Impact:* small — the permission is usually used or lost within a turn. *Fix scope:* hash the permission; add a codec slot.
PowerLSV cube creatures bucket (red / multicolor / colorless) — engine shortcuts (2026-09-27, `feature/cube-creatures-rmc`)10. **"Defending player"** (annihilator, Ragavan, Robber of the Rich, `rmc.DefendingPlayerSacrificesPermanents`) is the single opponent (two-player engine).

5 EoE pay-life shocklands admitted as plain untapped dual lands — `enters_tapped` / `pay-2-life` replacement dropped on BOTH engines (round-60 phase 1; activated-mana-ability cross-engine divergence CLOSED round-62)**What the shortcut is**: the production-deck trajectory-parity loader now admits the 5 EoE pay-life shocklands — **Breeding Pool, Watery Grave, Stomping Ground, Godless Shrine, Sacred Foundry** — as plain untapped dual-mana lands (a `CardDef(card_type="Land", mana_produced=<sorted dual>)`, the exact shape the basic-land arm emits, minus the `"Basic"` supertype gate). The real Magic card carries the replacement "As this land enters, you may pay 2 life. If you don't, it enters tapped." The live `OracleParserCardSource` **never structures that replacement at all** — it flattens each shockland to `produces={c1,c2}` + `enters_tapped=False` + zero abilities (verified round-60 against the live parser). The CardDef bridge has no `enters_tapped` field and Rust's `register_printing` has no land tapped-entry path, so the rider is dropped a SECOND time symmetrically. Net: the shockland is modeled as a vanilla untapped dual on BOTH engines — no pay-life decision, no tapped-entry, ever.
5 EoE pay-life shocklands admitted as plain untapped dual lands — `enters_tapped` / `pay-2-life` replacement dropped on BOTH engines (round-60 phase 1; activated-mana-ability cross-engine divergence CLOSED round-62)**Impact estimate**: **+5 cards / +18,065 cumulative 17lands decks** (Breeding Pool 4,712 + Watery Grave 4,226 + Stomping Ground 3,859 + Godless Shrine 2,937 + Sacred Foundry 2,331) unblocked into the production-deck bench, **0 strength cost** (no engine behavior changes; this is a bench-coverage admit, not a rules change). This is the entire *clean* realizable yield of the non-basic-land lever; the roadmap's remaining ~16,510-deck tail (the other 18) is gated behind the deferred Station / activated-ability / static / clone subsystems, not behind this substrate.

Documented shortcuts (docs/SEARCH_LIMITATIONS.md)

Rust-parity-pinned lossy legacy spells**What the shortcut is.** The compositional phrase grammar models "target creature or planeswalker", "counter target spell unless its controller pays {N}", and other surfaces faithfully, but five Edge-of-Eternities-era spells were claimed earlier through lossy legacy recognizers (planeswalker target arm dropped, pay-or-counter tax dropped, riders dropped, or only one of several modes kept) and their simplified models are pinned by cross-engine parity tests against the Rust engine: Divert Disaster, Don't Make a Sound, Archenemy's Charm, Scorching Dragonfire, Break Down the Door (plus Get Out / Untimely Malfunction for the single-parseable-mode modal fallback). While one of those names is being parsed the compositional grammar is switched off, so they keep the legacy models. Every other card with the same printed surfaces (including the cube's Mana Leak, Sear, Baleful Mastery, Unholy Heat, Mine Collapse, …) now parses faithfully, and the single-parseable-mode fallback no longer claims non-legacy modal spells (Suplex, Sheoldred's Edict must parse every mode).

Documented shortcuts (docs/SEARCH_LIMITATIONS.md)

Delirium and card-type counting (2026-09-28, `feature/cube-fixes-1`)Every "card types among cards in <zone>" count now goes through `mtg_bot.effects.card_types` (`card_types_of`, `count_card_types`, `delirium_active`): Delirium at both predicate tiers (`state_predicates.Delirium` for trigger gates, `conditions.DeliriumActive` for statics / "instead if" spell riders / activation restrictions — both carry the printed `min_card_types=4` and delegate to the one function), the Lhurgoyfs, Ursine Monstrosity, Keen-Eyed Curator, Occult Epiphany and Atraxa. What was wrong before: the delirium type set listed only the pre-2024 name "Tribal" (a Kindred card counted for nothing), each goyf / Ursine / Curator / Epiphany / Atraxa helper carried its own type tuple, and a card whose printing was still a back face / split half off the stack would have been read by that face. The shared helper folds Tribal into Kindred, unions a split card's halves (CR 709.4), reads a DFC by its front face (CR 712.8a — an MDFC land such as Shatterskull Smashing is a *sorcery* card in a graveyard, so it does NOT give delirium a land), reads an adventurer by its normal characteristics (CR 715.4) and skips tokens / spell copies (not cards).

Rust-parity-pinned lossy legacy spells**What the shortcut is.** The compositional phrase grammar models "target creature or planeswalker", "counter target spell unless its controller pays {N}", and other surfaces faithfully, but five Edge-of-Eternities-era spells were claimed earlier through lossy legacy recognizers (planeswalker target arm dropped, pay-or-counter tax dropped, riders dropped, or only one of several modes kept) and their simplified models are pinned by cross-engine parity tests against the Rust engine: Divert Disaster, Don't Make a Sound, Archenemy's Charm, Scorching Dragonfire, Break Down the Door (plus Get Out / Untimely Malfunction for the single-parseable-mode modal fallback). While one of those names is being parsed the compositional grammar is switched off, so they keep the legacy models. Every other card with the same printed surfaces (including the cube's Mana Leak, Sear, Baleful Mastery, Unholy Heat, Mine Collapse, …) now parses faithfully, and the single-parseable-mode fallback no longer claims non-legacy modal spells (Suplex, Sheoldred's Edict must parse every mode).

PowerLSV cube "glue" bucket — deliberate simplifications (2026-09-27, `feature/cube-glue`)The last sixteen normal-layout cube cards (Chandra, Torch of Defiance; Oko, Thief of Crowns; Wrenn and Six; Ugin, Eye of the Storms; Kaito, Bane of Nightmares; Nissa, Who Shakes the World; Tamiyo, Collector of Tales; Comet, Stellar Pup; Shelldock Isle; Coalition Relic; Mana Drain; Fear of Missing Out; Mawloc; Cloak and Dagger, Entwined; Tidehollow Sculler; Gleemox). Engine code: `src/mtg_bot/effects/generic/cube_glue.py`, `src/mtg_bot/player_protections.py`, `src/mtg_bot/cube_glue_statics.py`, hooks in `turn.py` / `simulate.py` / `search/engine_adapter.py` (step hooks only) / `actions.py` / `legal.py` / `game.py`; grammar: `src/mtg_bot/cards/parser/cube_glue_grammar.py` (last `_parse_effect` fallback, switched off for EoE-only printings through the shared `creature_rmc_grammar` guard). Kaito, Bane of Nightmares and Fear of Missing Out are also Duskmourn printings, so -- like Enduring Innocence in the W/G bucket -- they become claimed in the `eoe` / `all` pools too; no other EoE printing's parse changes.
Emblems as static sources and printing-level grants**Where:** `game._static_bonuses` / `_layer6_entries_for` scan `state.emblems`; `CreateEmblemWithAbilities.static_abilities` / `printing_fields`; `StaticScope.CARD_TYPE_PREFIX` (noncreature card-type scope); `CardPrinting.grants_retrace_to` (`graveyard_casting_wg.retrace_grant_filters`). **What:** emblem anthems (Kaito's Ninjas, Nissa's indestructible lands) and Wrenn and Six's retrace grant. Retrace keeps the W/G bucket's notes (the discarded land is chosen with `choose_discard`).

Documented shortcuts (docs/SEARCH_LIMITATIONS.md)

Printed alternative costs share the `cast_for_free` action variant**What the shortcut is.** CR 118.9 alternative costs (Force of Will, Daze, Force of Negation / Vigor, Snuff Out, Mine Collapse, Baleful Mastery, Overload on Damn / Winds of Abandon) ride the casting substrate's existing `CastSpell(cast_for_free=True)` variant — the same one `alt_casting`'s pitch costs and conditional free casts use — so there is ONE cast-time alternative-cost path and the action encoding is unchanged (the codec already has a `cast_for_free` slot). The variant means "cast for an alternative cost" rather than naming WHICH one: a free-cast permission wins, and when a card prints several payable alternatives the caster's agent picks among them with `choose_mode` inside the cast. No printed card in either pool has two payable alternatives at once, so today the variant is unambiguous. Two further approximations: (1) `search/_player_capabilities.py`'s priority short-circuit only checks mana costs, so with that heuristic enabled a player whose only castable card is a free-cast (e.g. Force of Will with no untapped lands) can be skipped; (2) when several candidates can pay an alternative cost the pick reuses existing hooks: `choose_discard` for the exiled hand card (as `alt_casting.pay_pitch_cost` does), `choose_sacrifice` for the returned / sacrificed permanent.

Cube lands (line-composed land grammar): automatic mana payment, hand abilities, life-costed taps — 2026-09-27, `feature/cube-lands`1. **Automatic payment only uses a land's `produces` set.** Lands built by the line-composed grammar set `mana_only_from_produces=True`: a land contributes to `can_pay_cost` / `auto_tap_for_cost` only through its free (or life-costed) `{T}: Add` production. Mana abilities with any other cost or shape — Gaea's Cradle / Tolarian Academy (scaling), Mishra's Workshop (spend restriction), Sunken Ruins (filter, `{U/B}` input), Gemstone Mine (counter cost), Starting Town's `{T}, Pay 1 life: Add one mana of any color`, Arena of Glory's exert ability — are explicit mana abilities, usable only by activating them (which `legal_actions` offers only in a sorcery window, like every activated ability) and floating the mana. So none of them can pay for an instant-speed cast.

5 EoE pay-life shocklands admitted as plain untapped dual lands — `enters_tapped` / `pay-2-life` replacement dropped on BOTH engines (round-60 phase 1; activated-mana-ability cross-engine divergence CLOSED round-62)**What the shortcut is**: the production-deck trajectory-parity loader now admits the 5 EoE pay-life shocklands — **Breeding Pool, Watery Grave, Stomping Ground, Godless Shrine, Sacred Foundry** — as plain untapped dual-mana lands (a `CardDef(card_type="Land", mana_produced=<sorted dual>)`, the exact shape the basic-land arm emits, minus the `"Basic"` supertype gate). The real Magic card carries the replacement "As this land enters, you may pay 2 life. If you don't, it enters tapped." The live `OracleParserCardSource` **never structures that replacement at all** — it flattens each shockland to `produces={c1,c2}` + `enters_tapped=False` + zero abilities (verified round-60 against the live parser). The CardDef bridge has no `enters_tapped` field and Rust's `register_printing` has no land tapped-entry path, so the rider is dropped a SECOND time symmetrically. Net: the shockland is modeled as a vanilla untapped dual on BOTH engines — no pay-life decision, no tapped-entry, ever.
5 EoE pay-life shocklands admitted as plain untapped dual lands — `enters_tapped` / `pay-2-life` replacement dropped on BOTH engines (round-60 phase 1; activated-mana-ability cross-engine divergence CLOSED round-62)**Why it's OK**: the drop is **symmetric** — the parser flattens the printing identically before either engine sees it, so Python and Rust materialize the *same* untapped dual and round-trip **byte-equal**. Pinned at two levels: (1) static — 3 cross-engine bridge pins build the real Stomping Ground / Watery Grave / Breeding Pool CardDefs and assert `compare_fields() == []`; (2) **activated** (round-62 N1, the level round-61 N3 showed was missing) — an activated-mana-ability cross-engine pin drives `activate_ability` for EACH color index of all 5 real shocklands on BOTH engines and asserts a byte-equal pool (see the ✅ CLOSED round-62 block below); plus 1 genuine real-EoE probe drives real 17lands archetype 30 (Stomping Ground + Watery Grave) through `attack_all` divergence-free. The bench's `attack_all` strategy never makes the pay-life choice and never reads a land's tapped-state for a decision, so the *replacement* simplification is inert under the coverage it unlocks. This is the **round-39 Ward precedent** exactly (`CardDef bridge filter drops creatures with dynamic_pt_formula / ward_cost`, this doc above): a rider the bridge drops symmetrically, bit-equal under the bench play strategy, shipped blocked-at-fidelity rather than as a latent inter-engine divergence. (The activated-mana-ability path itself was a real latent divergence until round-62 fixed it — see the CLOSED block below.)
5 EoE pay-life shocklands admitted as plain untapped dual lands — `enters_tapped` / `pay-2-life` replacement dropped on BOTH engines (round-60 phase 1; activated-mana-ability cross-engine divergence CLOSED round-62)**Impact estimate**: **+5 cards / +18,065 cumulative 17lands decks** (Breeding Pool 4,712 + Watery Grave 4,226 + Stomping Ground 3,859 + Godless Shrine 2,937 + Sacred Foundry 2,331) unblocked into the production-deck bench, **0 strength cost** (no engine behavior changes; this is a bench-coverage admit, not a rules change). This is the entire *clean* realizable yield of the non-basic-land lever; the roadmap's remaining ~16,510-deck tail (the other 18) is gated behind the deferred Station / activated-ability / static / clone subsystems, not behind this substrate.

Subtlety removes a spell from mid-stack by index; Deep-Cavern Bat's hand exile**What the shortcut is.** Stack targets are `("stack", index)` pairs, so when Subtlety pulls a spell out from under other stack items, the engine re-indexes those items' `targets` above the removed spell; nothing else stores stack indices today, but a future effect that does would need the same fix-up. The owner's top/bottom choice goes through `choose_yes_no`. Deep-Cavern Bat's pick goes through `choose_card_from_opponent_hand`, and the card returns to its owner's hand (not the battlefield) through the base's until-leaves release hook.

Documented shortcuts (docs/SEARCH_LIMITATIONS.md)

Cube lands (line-composed land grammar): automatic mana payment, hand abilities, life-costed taps — 2026-09-27, `feature/cube-lands`1. **Automatic payment only uses a land's `produces` set.** Lands built by the line-composed grammar set `mana_only_from_produces=True`: a land contributes to `can_pay_cost` / `auto_tap_for_cost` only through its free (or life-costed) `{T}: Add` production. Mana abilities with any other cost or shape — Gaea's Cradle / Tolarian Academy (scaling), Mishra's Workshop (spend restriction), Sunken Ruins (filter, `{U/B}` input), Gemstone Mine (counter cost), Starting Town's `{T}, Pay 1 life: Add one mana of any color`, Arena of Glory's exert ability — are explicit mana abilities, usable only by activating them (which `legal_actions` offers only in a sorcery window, like every activated ability) and floating the mana. So none of them can pay for an instant-speed cast.
Cube lands (line-composed land grammar): automatic mana payment, hand abilities, life-costed taps — 2026-09-27, `feature/cube-lands`6. **Hybrid filter input.** Sunken Ruins' `{U/B}` cost is paid by any mana (the existing `ManaCost.hybrid` "treated as generic-1" simplification).
